title: Non Overlapping Intervals
description:
Given intervals [start, end] in arbitrary order, remove as few as possible so the remaining intervals do not overlap. Each interval is half-open: it includes its start time but not its end time, so [1,2] and [2,3] can coexist. Return the minimum count removed, not the surviving ranges. An empty input needs zero removals.

Choose the interval that finishes first among overlapping options. Finishing earlier leaves at least as much room for every later interval as finishing later; therefore it is never worse to keep the earlier end. Sort by ascending end, breaking ties by ascending start, and accept a range only when its start is at least the end of the last accepted one.

Endpoints may be negative, and every input interval has positive duration. Deleting one wide interval can be better than deleting many small intervals contained in it; simply keeping the earliest starting meeting would be wrong. Tied end times need no special answer rule because only the number of removals is returned.

Example 1:

Input: intervals = [[1,2],[2,3],[3,4],[1,3]]
Output: 1

Example 2:

Input: intervals = [[1,2],[1,2],[1,2]]
Output: 2

Example 3:

Input: intervals = []
Output: 0

Constraints:

  • 0 <= intervals.length <= 100,000
  • -1,000,000 <= start < end <= 1,000,000
  • Each input interval has exactly two integer endpoints.

exampleTestCases.explanation: Remove [1,3] to keep three compatible ranges.
Only one identical interval can remain.
